title: Firebase Crashlytics API

deleteCrashReports.description: Enqueues a request to permanently remove crash reports associated with the specified user. All reports belonging to the specified user will be deleted typically within 24 hours of receiving the crash report.

name.description: Required. Resource name for user reports, in the format: projects/ PROJECT_IDENTIFIER/apps/APP_ID/users/USER_ID/crashReports - PROJECT_IDENTIFIER: The Firebase project's project number (recommended) or its project ID. Learn more about using project identifiers in Google's [AIP 2510 standard](https://google.aip.dev/cloud/2510). - APP_ID: The globally unique, Firebase-assigned identifier for the Firebase App. This is not your package name or bundle ID. Learn how to [find your app ID](https://firebase.google.com/support/faq/#find-app-id). - USER_ID: The user ID set using the Crashlytics SDK. Learn how to [set user identifiers](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/customize-crash-reports#set-user-ids).

list.description: List all of the available reports.

granularity.description: Optional. The report response will contain one data point per time grain. If omitted, the report will contain a single data point for the complete interval.
enumDescriptions: Returns a single interval for the requested time range.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous call. The page token is only valid for the exact same set of filters, which must also be sent in subsequent requests. This token is valid for 10 minutes after the first request.

filter.operatingSystem.displayNames.description: Only counts events in the given operating system and version. This string matches OperatingSystem.display_name. Format: "osName (osVersion)" e.g. "Android (11)". or just "osName" for all versions, e.g. simply "iPadOS".

filter.browser.displayNames.description: Optional. Only count events from the given browser. This string matches Browser.display_name. Format: "name (display_version)" e.g. "Chrome (123)", or just "name" for all possible versions, e.g. simply "Chrome".

filter.issue.signals.description: Optional. Only returns issues currently marked with the given signals. This field matches [Issue.signals.signal].
enumDescriptions: Indicates an issue that is impacting end users early in the app session.
Indicates previously closed issues which have been detected again.
Indicates issues impacting some end users multiple times.

filter.issue.content.description: Optional. A space separated list of filter terms matched against the contents of the issue. Contents include the title and the stack trace. Matches must begin at alphanumeric tokens, i.e., 'util.Sorted' matches 'java.util.SortedSet' but not 'myutil.SortedArray'. The filter matches if all filter terms match. All non-alphanumeric characters are ignored for matching. Filtering is assumed to be prefix-search and order-independent unless phrases are surrounded by "". Any terms contained in quotes are searched using exact-match (given filter term "foo", we will not return "foobar"), and must appear in the order given exactly. To get order-dependence but prefix-search, use a * within the quotes ("abc foo*" will match "abc foobar", but not "foo abc" "abcd foobar", or "abc xyz foobar").

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of result groups to return. If omitted, defaults to 25.

filter.device.displayNames.description: Only counts events from the given Device model. This string matches Device.display_name. Format: "manufacturer (model)" e.g. "Google (Pixel 6)", or just "manufacturer" for all possible models, e.g. simply "Google". Note that a device's marketing_name field can not be used for filtering.

filter.issue.id.description: Optional. Only counts events in the given issue ID. This field matches [Issue.id].

filter.interval.endTime.description: Optional. Exclusive end of the interval. If specified, a Timestamp matching this interval will have to be before the end.

filter.issue.variantId.description: Optional. Only counts events for the given issue variant ID. This field matches [IssueVariant.id].

filter.device.formFactors.description: Only counts events from devices with the given form factor (e.g. phone or tablet).
enumDescriptions: Includes mobile phones, small foldables and other form factors not fitting the other categories.
Includes both watches and other wearables.

name: firebasecrashlytics
description: This service provides an API for mobile app developers to request deletion of user's crash reports.

displayName.description: Browser name and version number. Formatted to be suitable for passing to BrowserFilter.

tracks.description: Indicates releases which have artifacts that are currently available in the Play Store to the target audience of the track. Versions may be available in multiple tracks.

displayName.description: Compound readable string containing both display and build versions. Format: "display_version (build_version)" e.g. "1.2.3 (456)". This string can be used for filtering with the VersionFilter.display_name field.

displayVersion.description: Readable version string, e.g. "1.2.3". On Android, strictly the same as "version name". On iOS, strictly the same as "version number" or CFBundleShortVersionString.

buildVersion.description: Mobile only. One display_version can have many build_version. On Android, strictly the same as "version code". On iOS, strictly the same as "build number" or CFBundleVersion.

metrics.description: Scalar metrics will contain a single object covering the entire interval, while time-dimensioned graphs will contain one per time grain.

subgroups.description: When applicable, this field contains additional nested groupings. For example, events can be grouped by operating system and by operating system version.

ReportGroup.description: A group of results in an EventReport. In any report, the group_parent field is strictly the same type for all of the groups in any collection.

totalSize.description: Output only. The total number of groups retrievable by the request.

name.description: The name of the report. Format: "projects/{project}/apps/{app_id}/reports/{report}".

displayName.description: Output only. The displayable title of the report.

nextPageToken.description: Output only. A page token used to retrieve additional report groups. If this field is not present, there are no subsequent pages available to retrieve.

groups.description: Aggregate event statistics in the report will be grouped by a dimension, such as by issue or by version. The response contains one element per group, and all ReportGroup messages will have the same parent field.

usage.description: Usage instructions for the report with a description of the result metrics. This field contains a description of the underlying query and describes the expected response data with any known caveats. This string can be displayed in the UI of any integration that offers comprehensive access to all Crashlytics reports.

Report.description: Response message for the GetReport method. A report consists of the results of a query over an application's events. The events may be filtered by various criteria defined in the filters proto. The result will consist of a number of paginated groups, of a type relevant to the report such as issues or device models.

endTime.description: The end of the interval covered by the computation.

startTime.description: The start of the interval covered by the computation.

sessionsCount.description: The number of distinct sessions in the set of events.

eventsCount.description: The total count of events in the interval.

impactedUsersCount.description: The number of distinct users in the set of events.

IntervalMetrics.description: A set of computed metric values for a time interval

title.description: Output only. Immutable. Caption title. This is usually a source file or method name.

enumDescriptions: Non-fatal event, such as a caught Java exception or NSError on iOS.
Application not responding error, Android only.
errorType.description: Output only. Immutable. Indicates whether this issue is a crash, non-fatal exception, or ANR.

state.description: Output only. Indicates whether this issue is open, closed or muted. For details on how issue states change without user actions, see [Regressed Issues](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/troubleshooting?platform=ios#regressed-issues).
enumDescriptions: Issue muted. No alerts will be fired for this issue.

notesCount.description: Output only. The number of notes attached to an issue.

signals.description: Output only. Immutable. Distinctive characteristics assigned by the Crashlytics analyzer.

sampleEvent.description: Output only. The resource name for a sample event in this issue.

subtitle.description: Output only. Immutable. Caption subtitle. This is usually a symbol or an exception message.

firstSeenTime.description: Output only. Immutable. The first time this issue was seen.

uri.description: Output only. Provides a link to the Issue on the Firebase console. When this Issue is obtained as part of a Report, then the link will be configured with the same time interval and filters as the request.

name.description: Required. Output only. Immutable. Identifier. The name of the issue resource. Format: "projects/{project}/apps/{app}/issues/{issue}".

lastSeenTime.description: Output only. The most recent time this issue was seen.

firstSeenVersion.description: Output only. Immutable. The first app display_version in which this issue was seen, populated for mobile issues only.

stateUpdateTime.description: Output only. The time at which the issue state was last changed.

id.description: Output only. Immutable. Unique identifier for the issue.

lastSeenVersion.description: Output only. The most recent app display_version in which this issue was seen, populated for mobile issues only.

variants.description: Output only. Immutable. The top 12 variants (subgroups) within the issue. Variants group events within an issue that are very similar. A single result implies that the variant is the same as the parent issue. This field will be empty when multiple issues are requested. Request a single issue to list variants.

Issue.description: An issue describes a set of similar events that have been analyzed by Crashlytics and grouped together. All events within an issue will be of the same error_type: crash, non-fatal exception or ANR. All events within an issue will contain similar stack traces in their blamed thread.

targetCompleteTime.description: Target time to complete the delete crash reports operation.

DeleteUserCrashReportsResponse.description: Response message for the DeleteUserCrashReports method. All crash reports associated with the specified user will be deleted typically within 24 hours of receiving the crash report.

offset.description: The byte offset into the binary image that contains the code. Present for native frames.

symbol.description: The frame symbol after it has been deobfuscated or symbolicated. The raw symbol from the device if it could not be hydrated.

blamed.description: True when the Crashlytics analysis has determined that this frame is likely to be the cause of the error.

owner.description: One of DEVELOPER, VENDOR, RUNTIME, PLATFORM, or SYSTEM.

library.description: The display name of the library that includes the frame.

address.description: The address in the binary image which contains the code. Present for native frames.

file.description: The name of the source file in which the frame is found.

line.description: The line number in the file of the frame.

modificationState.description: Indicates if the OS has been modified or "jailbroken".

type.description: The OS type on Apple platforms (iOS, iPadOS, etc.).

displayName.description: Name and version number. Formatted to be suitable for passing to OperatingSystemFilter.

BatchUpdateIssuesResponse.description: Response message for the BatchUpdateIssues method.

issues.description: Issues updated in the same order as in BatchUpdateIssuesRequest.

blamed.description: True when the Crashlytics analysis has determined that the stacktrace in this error is where the fault occurred.

frames.description: The frames in the error's stacktrace.

code.description: Error code associated with the app's custom logged NSError.

queue.description: The queue on which the thread was running.

Error.description: A non-fatal error and its stacktrace, only from Apple apps.

BatchUpdateIssuesRequest.description: Request message for the BatchUpdateIssues method.

requests.description: Required. The request message specifying the resources to update. A maximum of 100 issues can be modified in a batch.

updateMask.description: Optional. The list of Issue fields to update. If this is set, the update_mask field in the UpdateIssueRequest messages must either be empty or match this field.

WebMetricsGroup.description: Represents a grouping for metrics specific to web applications.

id.description: The id of the web metrics group

Empty.description: A generic empty message that you can re-use to avoid defining duplicated empty messages in your APIs. A typical example is to use it as the request or the response type of an API method. For instance: service Foo { rpc Bar(google.protobuf.Empty) returns (google.protobuf.Empty); }

IssueVariant.description: A variant is a subgroup of an issue where all events have very similar stack traces. Issues may contain one or more variants.

sampleEvent.description: Output only. The resource name for a sample event in this variant.

uri.description: Output only. Provides a link to the variant on the Firebase console. When this variant is obtained as part of a Report, then the link will be configured with the same time interval and filters as the request.

id.description: Output only. Immutable. Distinct identifier for the variant.

type.description: The type of track (prod, internal, etc...).

title.description: User-generated or auto-generated name of the track. PROD and INTERNAL track types always have auto-generated names, e.g. "prod" and "internal" respectively. Tracks of type EARLY_ACCESS always have a user-generated name. Other track types do not have any guarantees, might have user-generated or auto-generated names.

PlayTrack.description: Describes a release track in the Play Developer Console.

ListNotesResponse.description: Response message for the ListNotes method.

nextPageToken.description: A pagination token to retrieve the next page of notes. If this field is not present, there are no subsequent notes.

notes.description: Returns notes ordered descending by the timestamp.

id.description: User id if provided by the app developer.

Exception.description: A Java or Javascript exception and its stacktrace. Only from Android or web apps.

nested.description: True for all but the last-thrown exception (i.e. the first record).

blamed.description: True when the Crashlytics analysis has determined that this thread is where the fault occurred.

exceptionMessage.description: A message associated with the exception.

frames.description: The frames in the exception's stacktrace.

sessionId.description: Unique identifier for the Firebase session.

eventTime.description: The start timestamp for the session event.

eventType.description: Session event type. The SDK only supports SESSION_START events at this time.

firstSessionId.description: The identifier of the first session since the last cold start. This id and the session_id will be the same for app launches.

sessionIndex.description: Indicates the number of sessions since the last cold start.

firebaseInstallationId.description: Uniquely identifies a device with Firebase apps installed.

FirebaseSessionEvent.description: Sessions recorded by the Firebase App Quality Sessions SDK.

IssueSignals.description: Distinctive characteristics assigned by the Crashlytics analyzer.

enumDescriptions: Indicates an issue that is impacting end users early in the app session.
Indicates previously closed issues which have been detected again.
Indicates issues impacting some end users multiple times.

Event.description: The message describing a single Crashlytics event. Related to BigQuery export schema, which can be found at [Export Crashlytics data to BigQuery](https://firebase.google.com/docs/crashlytics/bigquery-export#dataset-schema-crashlytics)

customKeys.description: Custom keys set by the developer during the session.

routePath.description: Output only. Web only. The route path of the web application when the event occurred, excluding query parameters and fragment.

sessionId.description: Unique identifier for the Firebase session.

appOrientation.description: App orientation at the time of the crash (portrait or landscape).

deviceOrientation.description: Device orientation at the time of the crash (portrait or landscape).

logs.description: Log messages recorded by the developer during the session.

issue.description: Details for the [Issue] assigned to this [Event].

processState.description: The state of the app process at the time of the event.

buildStamp.description: Metadata provided by the app's build system, including version control repository info.

receivedTime.description: Server timestamp that the event was received by Crashlytics.

eventTime.description: Device timestamp that the event was recorded.

breadcrumbs.description: Analytics events recorded by the analytics SDK during the session.

blameFrame.description: The stack trace frame blamed by Crashlytics processing. May not be present in future analyzer.

bundleOrPackage.description: The bundle name for iOS apps or the package name of Android apps. Format: "com.mycompany.myapp".

eventId.description: Output only. Immutable. The unique event identifier is assigned during processing.

threads.description: Application threads present at the time the event was recorded. Each contains a stacktrace. One thread will be blamed for the error.

issueTitle.description: The title of the issue in which the event was grouped. This is usually a source file or method name.

issueSubtitle.description: The subtitle of the issue in which the event was grouped. This is usually a symbol or an exception message.

issueVariant.description: Details for the [IssueVariant] assigned to this [Event].

exceptions.description: Android and web only. Exceptions that occurred during this event. Nested exceptions are presented in reverse chronological order, so that the last record is the first exception thrown.

name.description: Required. Output only. Immutable. Identifier. The name of the event resource. Format: "projects/{project}/apps/{app_id}/events/{event}".

user.description: End user identifiers for the device owner.

errors.description: Apple only. A non-fatal error captured by the iOS SDK and its stacktrace.

installationUuid.description: Unique identifier for the device-app installation. This field is used to compute the unique number of impacted users.

events.description: Returns one element per event, in descending order the by event timestamp.

nextPageToken.description: A pagination token to retrieve the next page of events. The next page will have earlier or later events depending on the request's ordering. If this field is not present, there are no subsequent events.

ListEventsResponse.description: Response message for the ListEvents method.

createTime.description: Output only. Time when the note was created.

author.description: Output only. The email of the author of the note.

body.description: Immutable. The body of the note.

logTime.description: Device timestamp when the line was logged.

Log.description: Developer-provided log lines recorded during the session.

frames.description: The frames in the thread's stacktrace.

crashAddress.description: The address of the signal that caused the application to crash. Only present on crashed native threads.

threadState.description: Output only. The state of the thread at the time the ANR occurred.
enumDescriptions: Thread was waiting with a timeout.
Thread was started, yet to run anything.
The thread was native and we could not heuristically determine that it was was waiting, so assume it's runnable.
We heuristically determined that the thread is waiting.

blamed.description: True when the Crashlytics analysis has determined that the stacktrace in this thread is where the fault occurred.

threadId.description: The id of the thread, only available for ANR threads.

sysThreadId.description: The system id of the thread, only available for ANR threads.

queue.description: The queue on which the thread was running.

signal.description: The name of the signal that caused the app to crash. Only present on crashed native threads.

crashed.description: True when the thread has crashed.

signalCode.description: The code of the signal that caused the app to crash. Only present on crashed native threads.

ListReportsResponse.description: Response method for the ListReports method. The response will always include all of the available reports.

reports.description: The report objects returned will contain their names and usage instructions, but include no results. Use the `GetReport` method to run the report and obtain the paged results.

issue.description: Required. The issue to update. The issue's `name` field is used to identify the issue to update. Format: "projects/{project}/apps/{app}/issues/{issue}".

updateMask.description: Optional. The list of Issue fields to update. Currently only "state" is mutable.

UpdateIssueRequest.description: Request message for the UpdateIssue method.

enumDescriptions: Includes mobile phones, small foldables and other form factors not fitting the other categories.
Includes both watches and other wearables.

model.description: The model name which is consistent with android.os.Build.MODEL, e.g. ("SPH-L710", "GT-I9300").

displayName.description: Full device name, suitable for passing to DeviceFilter. Format: "manufacturer (model)".

marketingName.description: Marketing name, most recognizable public form, e.g. "Pixel 6".

manufacturer.description: Device brand name which is consistent with android.os.Build.BRAND.

companyName.description: An invariant name of the manufacturer that submitted this product in its most recognizable public form, e.g. "Google".

Storage.description: Mobile device disk/flash usage. Not reported for all devices.

Breadcrumb.description: Analytics events recorded during the session.
